gentisin: A tasteless, yellow, crystalline substance, obtained from the gentian; -- called also gentianin.
gestant: Bearing within; laden; burdened; pregnant. "Clouds gestant with heat." Mrs. Browning.
gemmeous: Pertaining to gems; of the nature of gems; resembling gems. Pennant.
geometrical: Pertaining to, or according to the rules or principles of, geometry; determined by geometry; as, a geometrical solution of a problem. Note: Geometric is often used, as opposed to algebraic, to include processes or solutions in which the propositions or principles of geometry are made use of rather than those of algebra.
geometrically: According to the rules or laws of geometry.
gelid: Cold; very cold; frozen. "Gelid founts." Thompson.
gemitores: A division of birds including the true pigeons.
geological: Of or pertaining to geology, or the science of the earth.
gear: 1. Clothing; garments; ornaments. Array thyself in thy most gorgeous gear. Spenser. 2. Goods; property; household stuff. Chaucer. Homely gear and common ware. Robynson (More's Utopia) 3. | 1. To dress; to put gear on; to harness. 2. (Mach.) To provide with gearing. Double geared, driven through twofold compound gearing, to increase the force or speed; -- said of a machine.
geographical: Of or pertaining to geography. Geographical distribution. See under Distribution. -- Geographic latitude (of a place), the angle included between a line perpendicular or normal to the level surface of water at rest at the place, and the plane of the equator;
geth: the original third pers. sing. pres. of Go. (old) Chaucer.
gelding: A castrated animal; -- usually applied to a horse, but formerly used also of the human male. They went down both into the water, Philip and the gelding, and Philip baptized him. Wyclif (Acts viii. 38).
genethlialogy: Divination as to the destinies of one newly born; the act or art of casting nativities; astrology.
gesticulation: 1. The act of gesticulating, or making gestures to express passion or enforce sentiments. 2. A gesture; a motion of the body or limbs in speaking, or in representing action or passion, and enforcing arguments and sentiments. Macaulay. 3. Antic tricks or motions. B. Jonson.
geothermometer: A thermometer specially constructed for measuring temperetures at a depth below the surface of the ground.
gesture: 1. Manner of carrying the body; position of the body or limbs; posture. (old) Accubation, or lying down at meals, was a gesture used by many nations. Sir T. Browne. 2. | To accompany or illustrate with gesture or action; to gesticulate. It is not orderly read, nor gestured as beseemeth. Hooker.
gelable: Capable of being congealed; capable of being converted into jelly.
generality: 1. The state of being general; the quality of including species or particulars. Hooker. 2. That which is general; that which lacks specificalness, practicalness, or application; a general or vague statement or phrase. Let us descend from generalities to particulars. Landor. The glittering and sounding generalities of natural right which make up the Declaration of Independence.
geochemistry: The study of the chemical composition of, and of actual or possible chemical changes in, the crust of the earth. -- Ge`o*chem"ic*al (#), a. --Ge`o*chem"ist (#), n.
gender: 1. Kind; sort. (old) "One gender of herbs." Shak. 2. Sex, male or female. [Obs. or Colloq.] 3. (Gram.) A classification of nouns, primarily according to sex; and secondarily according to some fancied or imputed quality associated with sex. Gender is a grammatical distinction and applies to words only. Sex is natural distinction and applies to living objects. R. Morris.
gern: To grin or yawn. (old) "[/He] gaped like a gulf when he did gern." Spenser.
gentlehearted: Having a kind or gentle disposition. Shak. -- Gen"tle-heart`ed*ness, n.
gently: In a gentle manner. My mistress gently chides the fault I made. Dryden.
gemul: A small South American deer (Furcifer Chilensis), with simple forked horns. [Written also guemul.]
geophagist: One who eats earth, as dirt, clay, chalk, etc.
genuflect: To bend the knee, as in worship.
gerah: A small coin and weight; 1-20th of a shekel. Note: The silver gerah is supposed to have been worth about three cents; the gold about fifty-four cents; the weight equivalent to about thirteen grains.
geogony: The branch of science which treats of the formation of the earth.
geotropism: A disposition to turn or incline towards the earth; the influence of gravity in determining the direction of growth of an organ. Note: In plants, organs which grow towards the center of the earth are said to be positively geotropic, and those growing in the opposite direction negatively geotropic.
geometrician: One skilled in geometry; a geometer; a mathematician.
georgiumsidus: The planet Uranus, so named by its discoverer, Sir W. Herschel.
gelose: An amorphous, gummy carbohydrate, found in Gelidium, agar-agar, and other seaweeds.
gerundively: In the manner of a gerund; as, or in place of, a gerund.
genu: (a) The knee. (b) The kneelike bend, in the anterior part of the callosum of the brain.
geyser: A boiling spring which throws forth at frequent intervals jets of water, mud, etc., driven up by the expansive power of steam. Note: Geysers were first known in Iceland, and later in New Zealand. In the Yellowstone region in the United States they are numerous, and some of them very powerful, throwing jets of boiling water and steam to a height of 200 feet.
germicide: Destructive to germs; -- applied to any agent which has a destructive action upon living germs, particularly bacteria, or bacterial germs, which are considered the cause of many infectious diseases. -- n. A germicide agent.
geranine: 1. (Med.) A valuable astringet obtained from the root of the Geranium maculatum or crane's-bill. 2. (Chem.) A liquid terpene, obtained from the crane's-bill (Geranium maculatum), and having a peculiar mulberry odor. [Written also geranium.]
geniting: A species of apple that ripens very early. Bacon.
geometry: 1. That branch of mathematics which investigates the relations, properties, and measurement of solids, surfaces, lines, and angles; the science which treats of the properties and relations of magnitudes; the science of the relations of space. 2. A treatise on this science.
gee: 1. To agree; to harmonize. [Colloq. or Prov. Eng.] Forby. 2. Etym: [Cf. G. jü, interj., used in calling to a horse, It. giò, F. dia, used to turn a horse to the left.] To turn to the off side, or… | To cause (a team) to turn to the off side, or from the driver. [Written also jee.]
gearing: 1. Harness. 2. (Mach.) The parts by which motion imparted to one portion of an engine or machine is transmitted to another, considered collectively; as, the valve gearing of locomotive engine; belt gearing; esp., a train of wheels for transmitting and varying motion in machinery. Frictional gearing. See under Frictional.
gerund: 1. A kind of verbal noun, having only the four oblique cases of the singular number, and governing cases like a participle. 2. (AS. Gram.) A verbal noun ending in -e, preceded by to and usually denoting purpose or end; -- called also the dative infinitive;
gewgaw: A showy trifle; a toy; a splendid plaything; a pretty but worthless bauble. A heavy gewgaw called a crown. Dryden. | Showy; unreal; pretentious. Seeing his gewgaw castle shine. Tennyson.
gentlewoman: 1. A woman of good family or of good breeding; a woman above the vulgar. Bacon. 2. A woman who attends a lady of high rank. Shak.
genterie: Nobility of birth or of character; gentility. (old) Chaucer.
gentile: One of a non-Jewish nation; one neither a Jew nor a Christian; a worshiper of false gods; a heathen. Note: The Hebrews included in the term goyim, or nations, all the tribes of men who had not… | 1. Belonging to the nations at large, as distinguished from the Jews; ethnic; of pagan or heathen people. 2. (Gram.) Denoting a race or country; as, a gentile noun or adjective.
genealogy: 1. An account or history of the descent of a person or family from an ancestor; enumeration of ancestors and their children in the natural order of succession; a pedigree. 2. Regular descent of a person or family from a progenitor; pedigree; lineage.
geography: 1. The science which treats of the world and its inhabitants; a description of the earth, or a portion of the earth, including its structure, fetures, products, political divisions, and the people by whom it is inhabited. 2. A treatise on this science.
generically: With regard to a genus, or an extensive class; as, an animal generically distinct from another, or two animals or plants generically allied.
genteel: 1. Possessing or exhibiting the qualities popularly regarded as belonging to high birth and breeding; free from vulgarity, or lowness of taste or behavior; adapted to a refined or cultivated taste; polite; well-bred; as, genteel company, manners, address. 2. Graceful in mien or form; elegant in appearance, dress, or manner; as, the lady has a genteel person. Law. 3.
geniculate: Bent abruptly at an angle, like the knee when bent; as, a geniculate stem; a geniculate ganglion; a geniculate twin crystal. | To form joints or knots on. Cockeram.
gestic: 1. Pertaining to deeds or feats of arms; legendary. And the gay grandsire, skilled in gestic lore. Goldsmith. 2. Relating to bodily motion; consisting of gestures; -- said especially with reference to dancing. Carried away by the enthusiasm of the gestic art. Sir W. Scott.
gerant: The manager or acting partner of a company, joint-stock association, etc.
gem: 1. (Bot.) A bud. From the joints of thy prolific stem A swelling knot is raised called a gem. Denham. 2. A precious stone of any kind, as the ruby, emerald, topaz, sapphire, beryl, spinel, etc.,… | 1. To put forth in the form of buds. "Gemmed their blossoms." Milton. 2. To adorn with gems or precious stones. 3. To embellish or adorn, as with gems; as, a foliage gemmed with dewdrops.
genuflection: The act of bending the knee, particularly in worship. Bp. Stillingfleet.
gemel: Coupled; paired. Bars gemel (Her.), two barrulets placed near and parallel to each other. | 1. One of the twins. (old) Wyclif. 2. (Heb.) One of the barrulets placed parallel and closed to each other. Cf. Bars gemel, under Gemel, a. Two gemels silver between two griffins passant. Strype.
germogen: (a) A polynuclear mass of protoplasm, not divided into separate cells, from which certain ova are developed. Balfour. (b) The primitive cell in certain embryonic forms. Balfour.
geolatry: The worship of the earth. G. W. Cox. The Geological Series. Note: The science of geology, as treating of the history of the globe, involves a description of the different strata which compose its crust, their order of succession, characteristic forms of animal and vegetable life, etc.
gemmuliferous: Bearing or producing gemmules or buds.
geoduck: A gigantic clam (Glycimeris generosa) of the Pacific coast of North America, highly valued as an article of food.
gecarcinian: A land crab of the genus Gecarcinus, or of allied genera.
germanize: To make German, or like what is distinctively German; as, to Germanize a province, a language, a society. | To reason or write after the manner of the Germans.
geld: Money; tribute; compensation; ransom.(old) Note: This word occurs in old law books in composition, as in danegeld, or danegelt, a tax imposed by the Danes; weregeld, compensation for the life of a… | 1. To castrate; to emasculate. 2. To deprive of anything essential. Bereft and gelded of his patrimony. Shak. 3. To deprive of anything exceptionable; as, to geld a book, or a story; to expurgate.
gelsemine: An alkaloid obtained from the yellow jasmine (Gelsemium sempervirens), as a bitter white semicrystalline substance; -- called also gelsemia.
generator: 1. One who, or that which, generates, begets, causes, or produces. 2. An apparatus in which vapor or gas is formed from a liquid or solid by means of heat or chemical process, as a steam boiler, gas retort, or vessel for generating carbonic acid gas, etc. 3. (Mus.) The principal sound or sounds by which others are produced; the fundamental note or root of the common chord;
gesso: 1. Plaster of Paris, or gypsum, esp. as prepared for use in painting, or in making bas-reliefs and the like; by extension, a plasterlike or pasty material spread upon a surface to fit it for painting or gilding, or a surface so prepared. 2. A work of art done in gesso. (old)
gelidness: The state of being gelid; gelidity.
geognostical: Of or pertaining to geognosy, or to a knowledge of the structure of the earth; geological.
genian: Of or pertaining to the chin; mental; as, the genian prominence.
gentlemanhood: The qualities or condition of a gentleman. Thackeray.
gessoduro: A variety of gesso which when dried becomes hard and durable, often used in making bas-relief casts, which are colored and mounted in elaborate frames.
genital: Pertaining to generation, or to the generative organs. Genital cord (Anat.), a cord developed in the fetus by the union of portions of the Wolffian and Müllerian ducts and giving rise to parts of the urogenital passages in both sexes.
genetical: Pertaining to, concerned with, or determined by, the genesis of anything, or its natural mode of production or development. This historical, genetical method of viewing prior systems of philosophy. Hare.
gerlind: A salmon returning from the sea the second time. [Prov. Eng.]
gesticulate: To make gestures or motions, as in speaking; to use postures. Sir T. Herbert. | To represent by gesture; to act. B. Jonson.
genealogical: Of or pertaining to genealogy; as, a genealogical table; genealogical order. -- Gen`e*a*log"ic*al*ly, adv. Genealogical tree, a family lineage or genealogy drawn out under the form of a tree and its branches.
geisha: A Japanese singing and dancing girl.
geometric: Pertaining to, or according to the rules or principles of, geometry; determined by geometry; as, a geometrical solution of a problem. Note: Geometric is often used, as opposed to algebraic, to include processes or solutions in which the propositions or principles of geometry are made use of rather than those of algebra.

gestour: A reciter of gests or legendary tales; a story-teller. (old) Minstrels and gestours for to tell tales. Chaucer.
georgianarchitecture: British or British colonial architecture of the period of the four Georges, especially that of the period before 1800.
gemarist: One versed in the Gemara, or adhering to its teachings.
geminate: In pairs or twains; two together; binate; twin; as, geminate flowers. Gray.
gelt: Trubute, tax. (old) All these the king granted unto them . . . free from all gelts and payments, in a most full and ample manner. Fuller. | Gilding; tinsel. (old) Spenser.
genet: 1. (Zoöl.) One of several species of small Carnivora of the genus Genetta, allied to the civets, but having the scent glands less developed, and without a pouch. Note: The common genet (Genetta… | A small-sized, well-proportioned, Spanish horse; a jennet. Shak.
gentilly: In a gentle or hoble manner; frankly. (old) Chaucer.

geoscopy: Knowledge of the earth, ground, or soil, obtained by inspection. Chambers.
gentiopikrin: A bitter, yellow, crystalline substance, regarded as a glucoside, and obtained from the gentian.
getpenny: Something which gets or gains money; a successful affair. [Colloq.] Chapman.
gemote: A meeting; -- used in combination, as, Witenagemote, an assembly of the wise men.
georgian: 1. Of or pertaining to Georgia, in Asia, or to Georgia, one of the United States. 2. Of or relating to the reigns of the four Georges, kings of Great Britan; as, the Georgian era. | A native of, or dweller in, Georgia.
gentleness: The quality or state of being gentle, well-born, mild, benevolent, docile, etc.; gentility; softness of manners, disposition, etc.; mildness.
geck: 1. Scorn, derision, or contempt. [Prov. Eng.] 2. An object of scorn; a dupe; a gull. (old) To become the geck and scorn O'the other's villainy. Shak. | 1. To deride; to scorn; to mock. [Prov. Eng.] 2. To cheat; trick, or gull. (old) Johnson.
geometrid: Pertaining or belonging to the Geometridæ. | One of numerous genera and species of moths, of the family Geometridæ; -- so called because their larvæ (called loopers, measuring worms, spanworms, and inchworms) creep in a looping manner, as if…
geitonogamy: Fertilization of flowers by pollen from other flowers on the same plant.
gent: 1. Gentle; noble; of gentle birth. (old) All of a knight [who] was fair and gent. Chaucer. 2. Neat; pretty; fine; elegant. (old) Spenser. Her body gent and small. Chaucer.
generification: The act or process of generalizing. Out of this the universal is elaborated by generification. Sir W. Hamilton.
germane: Literally, near akin; hence, closely allied; appropriate or fitting; relevant. The phrase would be more germane to the matter. Shak. [An amendment] must be germane. Barclay (Digest).
geology: 1. The science which treats: (a) Of the structure and mineral constitution of the globe; structural geology. genethliac: Pertaining to nativities; calculated by astrologers; showing position of stars at one's birth. Howell. | 1. A birthday poem. 2. One skilled in genethliacs.
geocentrical: (a) Having reference to the earth as center; in relation to or seen from the earth, -- usually opposed to heliocentric, as seen from the sun; as, the geocentric longitude or latitude of a planet. (b) Having reference to the center of the earth.
gerontes: Magistrates in Sparta, who with the ephori and kings, constituted the supreme civil authority.
genially: 1. By genius or nature; naturally. (old) Some men are genially disposed to some opinions. Glanvill. 2. Gayly; cheerfully. Johnson.
gerocomy: That part of medicine which treats of regimen for old people.
gentlefolks: Persons of gentle or good family and breeding. Etym: [Generally in the United States in the plural form.] Shak.
gentianose: A crystallizable, sugarlike substance, with a slightly sweetish taste, obtained from the gentian.
gerrymander: To divide (a State) into districts for the choice of representatives, in an unnatural and unfair way, with a view to give a political party an advantage over its opponent. genitals: The organs of generation; the sexual organs; the private parts.
geocyclic: 1. Of, pertaining to, or illustrating, the revolutions of the earth; as, a geocyclic machine. 2. Circling the earth periodically.
genio: A man of a particular turn of mind. Tatler.
geez: The original native name for the ancient Ethiopic language or people. See Ethiopic.
geoselenic: Pertaining to the earth and moon; belonging to the joint action or mutual relations of the earth and moon; as, geoselenic phenomena.
gerous: A suffix signifying bearing, producing; as, calcigerous; dentigerous.
genappe: A worsted yarn or cord of peculiar smoothness, used in the manufacture of braid, fringe, etc. Simmonds.
geminy: Twins; a pair; a couple. (old) Shak.
germinant: Sprouting; sending forth germs or buds.
georgic: A rural poem; a poetical composition on husbandry, containing rules for cultivating lands, etc.; as, the Georgics of Virgil. | Relating to agriculture and rural affairs.
gecko: Any lizard of the family Geckonidæ. The geckoes are small, carnivorous, mostly nocturnal animals with large eyes and vertical, elliptical pupils. Their toes are generally expanded, and furnished with adhesive disks, by which they can run over walls and ceilings. They are numerous in warm countries, and a few species are found in Europe and the United States.
getup: General composition or structure; manner in which the parts of a thing are combined; make-up; style of dress, etc. [Colloq.] H. Kingsley.
genethliacs: The science of calculating nativities, or predicting the future events of life from the stars which preside at birth. Jhonson.
gentlemanlike: Of, pertaining to, resembling, or becoming, a gentleman; well- behaved; courteous; polite.
gelatigenous: Producing, or yielding, gelatin; gelatiniferous; as, the gelatigeneous tissues.
geniohyoid: Of or pertaining to the chin and hyoid bone; as, the geniohyoid muscle.
gean: A species of cherry tree common in Europe (Prunus avium); also, the fruit, which is usually small and dark in color.
george: 1. A figure of St. George (the patron saint of England) on horseback, appended to the collar of the Order of the Garter. See Garter. 2. A kind of brown loaf. (old) Dryden.
genitocrural: Pertaining to the genital organs and the thigh; -- applied especially to one of the lumbar nerves.
generalissimo: The chief commander of an army; especially, the commander in chief of an army consisting of two or more grand divisions under separate commanders; -- a title used in most foreign countries.
getterup: One who contrives, makes, or arranges for, anything, as a book, a machine, etc. [Colloq.] A diligent getter-up of miscellaneous works. W. Irving.
general: 1. Relating to a genus or kind; pertaining to a whole class or order; as, a general law of animal or vegetable economy. 2. generatrix: That which generates; the point, or the mathematical magnitude, which, by its motion, generates another magnitude, as a line, surface, or solid; -- called also describent.
geosynclinal: the downward bend or subsidence of the earth's crust, which allows of the gradual accumulation of sediment, and hence forms the first step in the making of a mountain range; -- opposed to geanticlinal.
gelatine: , Gel"a*tine (, n. Etym: [F. gélatine, fr. L. gelare to congeal. See Geal.] (Chem.) Animal jelly; glutinous material obtained from animal tissues by prolonged boiling. Specifically (Physiol.
genette: 1. (Zoöl.) One of several species of small Carnivora of the genus Genetta, allied to the civets, but having the scent glands less developed, and without a pouch. The Cape genet (G. felina), and the berbe (G.
geodetically: In a geodetic manner; according to geodesy.
generalized: Comprising structural characters which are separated in more specialized forms; synthetic; as, a generalized type.

georama: A hollow globe on the inner surface of which a map of the world is depicted, to be examined by one standing inside.
genial: 1. Contributing to, or concerned in, propagation or production; generative; procreative; productive. "The genial bed." Milton. Creator Venus, genial power of love. Dryden. 2. geat: The channel or spout through which molten metal runs into a mold in casting. [Written also git, gate.]
gentianine: A bitter, crystallizable substance obtained from gentian.

geraniaceous: Of or pertaining to a natural order of pants (Geraniaceæ) which includes the genera Geranium, Pelargonium, and many others.
generic: 1. (Biol.) Pertaining to a genus or kind; relating to a genus, as distinct from a species, or from another genus; as, a generic description; a generic difference; a generic name. 2. gemmary: A receptacle for jewels or gems; a jewel house; jewels or gems, collectively.
generation: 1. The act of generating or begetting; procreation, as of animals. 2. Origination by some process, mathematical, chemical, or vital; production; formation; as, the generation of sounds, of gases, of curves, etc. 3. That which is generated or brought forth; progeny; offspiring. 4. A single step or stage in the succession of natural descent; a rank or remove in genealogy.

geoponic: Pertaining to tillage of the earth, or agriculture.
geocronite: A lead-gray or grayish blue mineral with a metallic luster, consisting of sulphur, antimony, and lead, with a small proportion of arsenic.

gentleship: The deportment or conduct of a gentleman. (old) Ascham.

geniculation: 1. The act of kneeling. Bp. Hall. 2. The state of being bent abruptly at an angle.

geniality: The quality of being genial; sympathetic cheerfulness; warmth of disposition and manners.
gephyrean: Belonging to the Gephyrea. -- n. One of the Gerphyrea.
genitor: 1. One who begets; a generator; an originator. Sheldon. 2. pl. The genitals. (old) Holland.
genethliatic: One who calculates nativities. Sir W. Drummond.

gemmiferous: Producing gems or buds; (Biol.) multiplying by buds.
